about: Radio and intercom for chapter 11: the entry. Everything in the air is cued by what the capsule feels (the heat, the load, the cabin's temperature), so it stays right at any clock speed; Houston is not heard between the loss of the radio and its return. t = GET (seconds from liftoff). Original lines in the style of the Apollo air-to-ground; not quotes.

lines.text: America, Houston. You are go for separation. Your entry angle is right down the middle. We will see you on the water.
Ten seconds to separation. Hang on to your hats.
Separation. The Service Module is gone. Just the three of us and the heat shield now.
Coming round to entry attitude. Blunt end forward, heads down.
One minute to the interface. Everybody tight in your straps.
Entry interface. Four hundred thousand feet. Here we go.
There's the glow. Look at the windows. Pale, like a neon light.
Point oh five g. The computer has her.
It's orange now. We're inside a fireball. Bits of the shield going by like sparks.
White hot out there. I can feel it coming through the hatch. It's getting warm in here.
Six. Six and a half. Hold on. Hold on.
She's easing off. That was the worst of it. We are through the peak.
Cabin is up five degrees. The shield is doing its job.
America, Houston. Standing by. America, Houston. How do you read?
Houston, America. Loud and clear, and it is a beautiful day up here.
Roger, America. We have you on radar. Standing by for the drogues.
